bio: Steeped in tradition and brimming with regional charm, this establishment is staffed by a young and adept team who deliver pleasingly down-to-earth yet ambitious cuisine. While the friendly proprietress Emma Ambs, who hails from a family of restaurateurs in the next village, attentively manages the service, Simon Bantle (a veteran of various MICHELIN-starred kitchens) fuses hearty traditional fare with classic French recipes. The dishes are meticulously prepared, packed with flavour and delightfully unpretentious – think jellied veal tripe with fried potatoes, or braised ox cheeks with Ihringen pinot noir jus, served with creamed kohlrabi, kohlrabi purée and pommes dauphine.
